newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says meeting with India minister still on.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says meeting with India minister still on.

text.p: Pakistan said on Wednesday that Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan would hold talks with his Indian counterpart in New Delhi next week despite political turmoil in India.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters Ayub Khan had received an invitation from Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral to meet at the end of a Non-Aligned Movement ministerial conference on April 7-8.
But the spokesman said he was uncertain what affect the Indian domestic political crisis would have on the meeting.
The India crisis arose with the withdrawal of support by Congress party for Prime Minister H.K. Deve Gowda's colaition government. A parliamentary confidence motion is slated for April 11.
Pakistan's official APP news agency quoted Ayub Khan as saying on Tuesday that his talks with Gujral might be put off because of the looming confidence test.

The Pakistani spokesman would not say what subjects would be discussed at the meeting. Top foreign ministry officials of the one-time foes held four days of meetings in New Delhi on March 28-31 after a three-year standoff.
"But on our side, we are prepared to discuss all outstanding issues," he said.
The spokesman said the Pakistani side had urged India in the New Delhi talks to halt "repression" in the Indian-ruled two-thirds of the disputed Himalyan region of Kashmir.

"We pointed out that steps towards this end would help create a propitious climate for future negotiations between the two countries," he said. India is fighting a separatist Moslem revolt in its part of Jammu and Kashmir.
Pakistan controls the remaining third of the region, over which the two countries have fought two of their three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947.
